ai.summary: The agent runtime now prevents mechanical context compaction from firing when the pass would leave the history back at the trigger threshold, a state labeled "above_low_water". A new exported function, `automaticCompactionPostCeiling`, applies the same `COMPACTION_LOW_WATER` rule (85% of the threshold) to the actual result of a pass rather than just the predicted context. In `run-agent-step.ts`, this ceiling is passed as `maxPostTokens` to `compactMechanically`, causing the runtime to skip the pass and defer to the hard budget when the result is too large. This change addresses a production pattern where small BYOK windows with large fixed tool schemas caused the agent to repeatedly compact its own summary every few tool calls.

eli5.text: The assistant's internal memory management now double-checks its own summarization result to ensure it actually freed up enough space. Previously, the system would attempt to shrink its context whenever it approached a limit, but if the summarization left too much information behind, it would trigger the limit again just moments later, causing a rapid loop of unhelpful re-summarizing. This update stops that cycle by verifying the final size after the pass and skipping it if the result is still too large. For you, this means smoother and more reliable coding sessions, particularly when using a model with a smaller memory window, as the assistant will no longer stall while repeatedly trying to clear its own notes.
